'''Darius Myron Washington Jr.''' (born December 6, 1985) is an American-Macedonian former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[KB Peja|Peja]] of the [[Kosovo Basketball Superleague|Kosovo Superleague]].

He is a [[combo guard]] and played [[college basketball]] with the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|University of Memphis]]. He has also played with the [[NBA]]'s [[San Antonio Spurs]] and the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]'s [[Austin Toros]] in 2007. He also is the subject of a Phish song called The Line.

==Amateur career==
An AAU national champion at age 10,{{cn|date=June 2019}} Washington attended [[Edgewater High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.thetournament.com/news/darius-washington-jr-game-winner-against-memphis-alumni-was-poetic-justice | title = For Darius Washington Jr, game winner against Memphis alumni was poetic justice | website = [[The Basketball Tournament]] | via = thetournament.com | access-date = June 17, 2019 | archive-date = June 17, 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190617235720/https://www.thetournament.com/news/darius-washington-jr-game-winner-against-memphis-alumni-was-poetic-justice | url-status = dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Darius Washington, Jr. |url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Darius-Washington%2C%20Jr.-12643 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406080543/http://rivals.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Darius-Washington,%20Jr.-12643 |archive-date=April 6, 2012 |access-date=June 24, 2025 |publisher=Rivals.com |url-status=dead}}</ref> In his senior year, he played in an [[ESPN]] High School Showcase game against future NBA player [[Sebastian Telfair]].{{cn|date=June 2019}}

He went to [[University of Memphis]], where he earned Conference USA Rookie of the Year and freshman All-American honors on averages of 15.4 points per game and a team-best 3.8 assists. With no time remaining in the championship game of the 2005 Conference-USA tournament, Washington was given three free throws to overcome a 75–73 lead by the sixth-ranked [[University of Louisville|Louisville Cardinals]]. Although Washington was a 72-percent shooter, he missed two of the three foul shots, giving Louisville the win and an appearance in the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] while Washington and the Tigers' season would continue in the NIT, where they would reach the semifinal round.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?columnist=oneil_dana&id=4436714 Well-traveled Washington motors on]</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/tournaments/Post-Season/NIT-Tournament/33/Bracket/2005/323|title=NIT Tournament Bracket, Scores, Stats, Schedule – RealGM}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/ncaa/conferences/Conference-USA/9/Memphis/301/Rosters/2005|title = Memphis Rosters – RealGM}}</ref>

In his sophomore season at Memphis, Washington helped lead the #1-seeded Tigers to an [[Elite Eight]] appearance in the [[2006 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2006 NCAA tournament]], losing to eventual runner-up [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. He was named to the All-Conference USA first team and earned an honorable mention as an [[All-American]] by the [[Associated Press]].

==Professional career==
On April 25, 2006, Washington declared himself as an early entry candidate for the [[2006 NBA draft]]. Confident he would be drafted, he signed with a [[sports agent]] on June 26, two days before the draft, losing his eligibility to play in college. With analysts being skeptical on his reliability to play point guard, he was not drafted. Although analyst [[Dick Vitale]] and others believed Washington had a shot to make an NBA roster as a free agent,<ref>[https://www.espn.com/dickvitale/060628vitaleundrafted.html ESPN.com – Dick Vitale – Vitale's 2006 All-Undrafted Underclassmen team<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> he failed to do so after trying out with several teams during training camp.

===Europe===
He was later drafted by the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[D-League]], but he instead chose to sign with [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] of the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]]. In 2007, he led the [[ČEZ Basketball Nymburk|ČEZ Nymburk]] team to the [[National Basketball League (Czech Republic)|Czech Republic League]] title after leaving PAOK. He played in the [[ULEB Cup]] competition during the year with both clubs.

In January 2008, Washington signed a 2-year contract with the [[Euroleague]] club [[Aris BC|Aris Thessaloniki]], a team that competes in the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]]. He was released by Aris after one season. At the end of October 2008, he signed a contract with the [[Russian Basketball Super League|Russian Super League]] club [[PBC Ural Great|Ural Great Perm]].

In July 2009, he signed a contract with [[Galatasaray Cafe Crown]].<ref>[http://www.galatasaray.org/basketbol/erkek/haber/4230.php Darius Washington Galatasaray Cafe Crown'da]</ref>

In April 2010, he signed with [[Lottomatica Roma]] until the end of the season.

In 2011, he joined the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.elnuevodia.com/nuevopirata-1006417.html |title=Nuevo Pirata |access-date=2011-07-03 |archive-date=2013-11-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112110436/http://www.elnuevodia.com/nuevopirata-1006417.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the summer of 2011, he signed a contract with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]].

In January 2013, he joined Israeli side [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]], but only played 6 games with the team, averaging 11ppg and 1.3apg. Though highly praised in Eilat, his contract was bought out and in February, he moved to French side [[Le Mans Sarthe Basket|Le Mans]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/darius-washington-to-le-mans/ |title=Darius Washington to Le Mans |access-date=February 19, 2013 |archive-date=November 12, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112104053/http://www.court-side.com/news/blog/darius-washington-to-le-mans/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In July 2013, he joined [[Olin Edirne Basket]] in Turkey.<ref>[http://basketball.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/Darius_Washington_(ex_Le_Mans)_is_a_newcomer_at_Olin_Edirne/326551 Darius Washington (ex Le Mans) is a newcomer at Olin Edirne]</ref>

On June 23, 2014, he signed with his former team ČEZ Nymburk for the 2014–15 season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/czech-republic/123832/cez-nymburk-announces-darius-washington.html CEZ Nymburk announces Darius Washington]</ref>

On January 16, 2018, he returned to Greece and joined [[Iraklis Thessaloniki BC|Iraklis Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek A2 Basket League]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/Greece/news/522596/Iraklis-ink-Darius-Washington Iraklis ink Darius Washington]</ref>

On April 5, 2019, he signed with Macedonian basketball club [[KK Rabotnički|Rabotnički]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ekipa.mk/rabotnichki-ne-zapira-potpis-i-so-makedonetsot-vashington|title=Работнички не запира – потпис и со Македонецот Вашингтон | trans-title = Rabotnicki does not stop – a signature with the Macedonian Washington |website=ekipa.mk| date = April 5, 2019 |language=mk|access-date=April 5, 2019}}</ref>

On May 4, 2020, he signed with [[Phoenix Brussels]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Darius Washington signs with Brussels Basketball |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/darius-washington-signs-with-brussels-basketball/ |website=Sportando |access-date=May 5, 2020 |date=May 4, 2020}}</ref>

===The Basketball Tournament (TBT)===
In the summer of 2018, Washington competed in [[The Basketball Tournament 2018|The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]] for Team DRC. In three games, he averaged 15.0 points, 4.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 2.0 steals per game. His team was eliminated in Super 16 Round by Ram Nation.

In the summer of 2019, he also competed in [[The Basketball Tournament 2019|The Basketball Tournament]] on [[ESPN]]. In two games for Bluff City, he averages 12.5 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.0 assists and 1 steals per game. His team was eliminated in Round 2 of [[The Basketball Tournament 2019#Memphis Regional – Elma Roane Fieldhouse, Memphis, TN|Memphis Regional Tournament]] by Louisiana United.

===NBA===
Washington signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on October 1, 2007, and was assigned to the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA D-League]] in late November.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=100 Spurs assign Darius Washington to D-League]</ref> He was called up in early December to take [[Tony Parker]]'s spot on the roster while he healed from an injury; however, Washington was waived by the Spurs on December 28.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=227 Spurs waive Darius Washington]</ref> He appeared in 18 games for the Spurs where he averaged 2.9 points and 1.1 rebounds in 8.1 minutes.

He played with the [[Chicago Bulls]] during the 2008–09 NBA pre-season, but was waived by the team before the start of the regular season.

==Macedonian national team==
Washington was granted Macedonian citizenship {{when|date=May 2015}},<ref>[http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Darius_Washington/Czech-Republic/CEZ_Basketball_Nymburk/46092 Darius Washington basketball profile Nationality: FYR Macedonia-USA.]</ref> and he joined the [[Macedonian national basketball team]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT,ovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.playerID_53799.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.teamID_2604.html Eurobasket2009.org] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090901104511/http://www.eurobasket2009.org/en/cid_toT%2CovGDH2EaLKL67XnPo2.playerID_53799.compID_qMRZdYCZI6EoANOrUf9le2.season_2009.roundID_6328.teamID_2604.html |date=2009-09-01 }}</ref>

==In popular culture==
The song "The Line" by [[Phish]] was written about the missed free throws at the conclusion of the 2005 C-USA Championship game. The song premiered in Atlantic City, New Jersey on October 31, 2013. However, during the performance, Phish guitarist [[Trey Anastasio]] mistakenly referred to Washington as having played for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and the missed free throws as having taken place during the [[Final Four]].<ref>Trey Anastasio, 10/31/13</ref>
